en: Earth's seasons are caused by the 23.5-degree tilt of its rotational axis, not by its changing distance from the Sun.
The far side of the Moon receives just as much sunlight as the near side, but it is hidden from Earth's view.
Lightning often strikes the same tall place twice, with the Empire State Building averaging 25 strikes per year.
Soil is not just broken-down rocks, but also contains vital organic matter from decaying plants and living organisms like earthworms.
Clouds are made of tiny liquid water droplets or solid ice crystals, not invisible water vapor gas.
The Sun is not a ball of burning fire, but a giant sphere of plasma generating energy through nuclear fusion.
Most diamonds formed deep inside Earth from pure carbon under extreme pressure, long before plants existed to create coal.
Only the thin outer crust of a meteorite melts during atmospheric entry, leaving the interior rock completely cold.
Ocean tides are primarily caused by the gravitational pull of the Moon and the Sun, not by wind blowing on the water.
We see the same side of the Moon because it rotates on its axis at the exact same rate it orbits Earth.
High humidity means the air holds a lot of invisible water vapor, but rain only falls when that vapor condenses into heavy droplets.
Earthquakes occur when tectonic plates get stuck at their edges due to friction and suddenly release built-up energy, rather than sliding smoothly.
